minutes.headline: Board backed police carrying Narcan and asked the Board of Health to cede the farmers market to the Ag Commission.
minutes.summary: The board heard the Agricultural Commission ask to oversee the farmers market and for a small promotion budget. It heard the police and fire chiefs on Narcan, with members voicing strong support for equipping police. It opened the annual town meeting warrant, ratified a short-term note and accepted the Lane property deed with a condition, and reviewed regional transit plans and committee reports.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to send the Board of Health a letter supporting transfer of the farmers market to the Agricultural Commission, and asking for the regulations and adoption dates.
The board voted to accept the Lane property deed pending Town Counsel approval, with no restrictions contradicting the grant application, and ratified the short-term note for the purchase.
The board opened the annual town meeting warrant until March 23rd at 4 p.m.
The police and fire chiefs briefed the board on Narcan; members voiced support for equipping police, and training may be folded into other training.
The Agricultural Commission was told to prepare an informal promotion budget for the town manager; a gift account can be set up for donations.

why_it_matters: The Lane purchase is funded by short-term borrowing, with a state land grant reimbursing a share, so the town budget, mostly taxes, carries the rest until permanent financing.
Narcan for police would be a new start-up cost for training and initial stock, and the price per dose was heard to have risen, so it may reach a future public safety budget.
The open warrant is the window for placing articles before voters at annual town meeting.
watch_next: Warrant closes March 23rd at 4 p.m.; articles must be submitted by then.
The Board of Health's response on the farmers market regulations and adoption dates, and the Agricultural Commission's informal promotion budget.
